text:
The text contrasts the theme of inherent human evil with the theme of societal corruption. In William Golding's 'Lord of the Flies', the presentation suggests that savagery and evil are innate to humans, as evidenced by the boys' descent into chaos when removed from societal structures. Conversely, Jean-Jacques Rousseau’s philosophy presents the opposite view, arguing that humanity is naturally good and free, and that it is the constraints of society that corrupt individuals. While both texts address the nature of humanity and its relationship with civilization, they differ fundamentally in their conclusions: Golding sees civilization as a veneer over inherent darkness, whereas Rousseau sees civilization as the source of corruption over inherent goodness.

The organ that pumps blood is the heart.
